briefing.text: The deposited tables for this study (clinical sample table, MSK-IMPACT341/410 mutations, CNA and seg files) hold no miRNA expression and no normal-liver samples; every sample is a Tumor-class HCC or hepatocellular adenoma (LIAD/HCA). Confirm this by grepping for 'miR'/'MIR' and listing sample types. Under the benchmark convention, missing data alone does not make a hypothesis 'Not verifiable'. First decide whether the hypothesis is about this study's disease and cohort (HCC vs HCA). If it is, label it True or False from the study context and established biology, and say that this kind of evidence decided the label.
briefing.reason: The most likely error is defaulting to 'Not verifiable' because the miRNA measurements were not deposited. The grading convention treats on-topic claims as True/False.

briefing.text: Do not use copy-number gain at the miRNA host loci as a stand-in for miRNA upregulation (MIR452 at Xq28 within GABRE, MIR766 at Xq24 in SEPTIN6, MIR1180 at 17p11.2). The MSK-IMPACT panels cover these loci poorly or not at all, and there is no normal-liver comparator. Check whether these genes or loci appear in data_cna.txt or the .seg file. If they are absent or sparse, say so and do not treat CNA as evidence of expression.
briefing.reason: This stops an invalid proxy analysis from deciding the label.

briefing.text: The hypothesis is a compound claim: three miRNAs, each upregulated in both HCA and HCC compared with normal liver. It holds only if every part holds. If any miRNA is not upregulated in either tumour type (for example, up only in HCC, or down in HCA), the claim is False. Assess each miRNA-by-tissue comparison separately before you choose the label.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team noted that this cohort consists of exactly the two tumour types named in the hypothesis (HCC and hepatocellular adenoma), and treated that match as evidence the hypothesis is about this study, even though no miRNA data or normal liver are deposited. The task's convention says hypotheses from the source study are labelled True or False even when the tables lack the needed measurement, and Not verifiable is reserved for claims about a disease, cohort or data kind the tables do not cover at all. Does a study whose design is HCC versus HCA fit a hypothesis comparing HCC and HCA to normal liver? Does that change your method or your reading of the convention?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team treated the hypothesis as a compound claim (three miRNAs, each in two tumour types versus normal) and assessed each of the six comparisons separately. Your notes record no pitfalls checked. If you decide the hypothesis is about this study, how would you assess each part from study context and established biology, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team judged that the hypothesis's data type (miRNA expression profiling against normal liver) is wholly absent from a DNA-panel study of 19 tumours, and that this may mean the claim was attached from a different publication. The convention allows Not verifiable when the kind of data the hypothesis is about is not covered at all. What evidence, from the tables or study design, shows that this study itself plausibly measured miRNAs and normal liver? Does weighing that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team recorded that the samples were sequenced on targeted MSK-IMPACT341/410 DNA panels with no MIR genes in the CNA table. Your own weakest point is that your label rests on guessing whether the original finding was stated as-is or altered. What specific established biology or study context about these three miRNAs in each tumour type supports your decision for each of the six comparisons, and is that evidence strong enough to keep your label?

What is reported in the published literature about expression of miR-452, miR-766 and miR-1180 in hepatocellular adenoma and in hepatocellular carcinoma compared with normal liver tissue, for each miRNA and each tumour type separately?

questions.question: Have studies comparing hepatocellular adenoma with hepatocellular carcinoma using targeted DNA sequencing also reported miRNA expression profiling against normal liver in the same publication?
questions.why: Settles whether a miRNA-vs-normal claim plausibly comes from a HCC/HCA genomic study (True/False) or from a separate publication (Not verifiable), the core disagreement.

findings.question: What is reported in the published literature about expression of miR-452, miR-766 and miR-1180 in hepatocellular adenoma and in hepatocellular carcinoma compared with normal liver tissue, for each miRNA and each tumour type separately?
findings.answer: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: all 4 research calls (3 search, 1 contents) failed with HTTP 502 (Exa returned 403), so no page was read. Unverified recall from training knowledge only: HCC vs normal - miR-452 reported upregulated (oncogenic; e.g. targets SOX7, CDKN1B); miR-1180 reported upregulated (promotes proliferation via NF-kB/OTUD7B); miR-766 mixed reports (some describe miR-766-3p as down/tumour-suppressive in HCC). HCA vs normal - no recalled published data for any of the three miRNAs. Do not treat any of this as verified.
